title: The Outlaw Chemist Teaching People How to Make Drugs From Scratch
gist: Masked psychedelic educator William 'Willy' Myco built a six-figure creator business on 120+ drug-synthesis how-to videos — 96,000 YouTube followers and 14,500 Patreon subscribers — using a Pakistani university lab with claimed government research approval as regulatory cover, until both platforms terminated him after WIRED's inquiry. The story is a case study in decentralized DIY access forming as a direct counter-current to the clinical, regulated psychedelic-medicine industry, with contested science and threats from incumbent drug dealers attached.

insights.claim: A creator's 96,000-follower YouTube channel and 14,500-subscriber Patreon were both terminated within days of a journalist contacting the platforms for comment, showing press inquiry — not automated enforcement — is the trigger that actually removes borderline content businesses.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Platform policy enforcement on gray-zone content is reactive to media exposure, making journalistic attention a discrete tail risk for creator-economy revenue.
insights.quote: His YouTube channel, called “Willy’s World,” had over 96,000 followers but was taken down after WIRED reached out to the platform for comment.

insights.claim: YouTube's stated removal reason was not the drug content itself but its terms prohibiting new channels after a termination, meaning account-history violations can override an otherwise clean content record.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Platform bans propagate across accounts and time; creators who rebuild after a ban carry permanent latent termination risk regardless of subsequent compliance.
insights.quote: YouTube spokesperson Boot Bullwinkle said it was removed “under our terms of service, which prohibit creating new channels after a termination.”

insights.claim: Patreon has an explicit prohibition on works providing instructions for creating controlled substances or other recreational drugs, and enforced it via internal investigation after inquiry — a policy line that a whole category of harm-reduction content sits on the wrong side of.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Subscription platforms are not neutral rails for legally ambiguous educational content; policy risk should be priced into any creator business built on them.
insights.quote: Patreon prohibits works that provide instructions around the creation of controlled substances or other recreational drugs.
insights.locator: But shortly afterward, his Patreon account was taken down too

insights.claim: The creator's fallback plan after deplatforming is Discord plus his own website, illustrating that owned channels are the only durable infrastructure for content the mainstream platforms will eventually reject.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Deplatforming pushes audiences into unmoderated, unmonetizable venues — bad for platform ad revenue, good for self-hosted community software.
insights.quote: If he is unable to get Patreon to reconsider, Myco says he will simply continue his work through Discord and his website.
insights.locator: If he is unable to get Patreon to reconsider

insights.claim: The creator openly states the deplatforming vulnerability is why he concentrated effort on Patreon rather than YouTube — and then lost Patreon too, demonstrating that diversification within third-party platforms is not real diversification.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Creator-economy risk is correlated across platforms because policies converge; only owned distribution decorrelates it.
insights.quote: So if you’ve ever asked why I put all my energy into my patreon channel … this is why.

themes.theme: The creator business model behind the content

insights.claim: The business stacks multiple revenue lines beyond subscriptions — mushroom genetics sales, branded merchandise, consultancy for mushroom growers, and organized group vacations — with documents indicating annual revenue possibly well into six figures.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Niche subcultural creators monetize through product and community, not ad rates; the subscription is the funnel, not the business.
insights.quote: documents of last year’s revenue, shared with WIRED, indicate that he possibly earns well into the six figures
insights.locator: He refused to publicly state how much money he makes

insights.claim: Each synthesis video cost tens of thousands of dollars to produce, putting this content in a high-capex tier that a hobbyist cannot replicate and that requires sustained subscriber revenue to fund.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: High production cost is a moat but also a fragility — deplatforming immediately breaks the funding loop that pays the team.
insights.quote: Each video cost tens of thousands of dollars to produce, he says.
insights.locator: Next up, he plans to undermine an incoming US Drug Enforcement Administration ban

insights.claim: The creator's growth followed a discovery accident rather than a strategy: a single 2014 psilocybin-cultivation explainer filmed in a gas mask accrued thousands of subscribers unnoticed, prompting him to quit a well-paid pharmaceutical job in Boston.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Underserved taboo niches produce outsized organic distribution because no incumbent competes for them.
insights.quote: Several months later Myco logged back into his YouTube creator account and discovered “it had completely blown up,” accruing thousands of subscribers.
insights.locator: Myco says he went on to work for a pharmaceutical company

insights.claim: The audience is bound by identity rather than transaction — subscribers are branded the 'Trip Team family' and the creator runs annual group trips to Disney World and a Sedona 'Tripaween' event for 30-plus followers.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Identity-based community is what survives deplatforming — the audience follows the person to Discord, not the platform.
insights.quote: anointing his supporters as the “Trip Team family.”
insights.locator: Several months later Myco logged back into his YouTube creator account

insights.claim: To reduce prosecution risk the creator says he located a university laboratory in Pakistan that had government approval to produce psychedelics for scientific research, then filmed LSD, MDMA and 2C-B syntheses there — offshore research permits functioning as content-production cover.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Jurisdictional arbitrage on research licensing is a repeatable pattern; enforcement gaps between filming location and audience location are hard to close.
insights.quote: To minimize the threat of censure or even prosecution, Myco claims that in May 2024 he found a university laboratory in Pakistan, which apparently secured government approval to produce the psychedelics for scientific research.
insights.locator: So he decided to try to become the first person

insights.claim: The creator is explicitly planning to preempt an incoming US DEA scheduling ban on 7-OH, the opioid-like kratom compound, by publishing a synthesis video before the ban takes effect — treating regulation as a content trigger rather than a constraint.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Scheduling actions may now generate immediate open-source synthesis instructions, undermining the supply-suppression logic of prohibition.
insights.quote: So I think it’s time to film a synth video showing you how to make your own [7-OH] of the highest quality for next to nothing.
insights.locator: Next up, he plans to undermine an incoming US Drug Enforcement Administration ban

insights.claim: As hallucinogens move toward mainstream medicine, a countervailing movement is pushing the opposite direction — away from clinics, regulators and expensive trip-sitters toward radical self-sufficiency at home for pennies on the dollar.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: A free DIY substitute forming beneath the clinical psychedelic industry is a direct pricing threat to any therapy business charging clinic-level fees.
insights.quote: As hallucinogens edge closer to mainstream medicine, Myco is pushing in the opposite direction—away from clinics, regulators, and expensive trip-sitters, and toward radical self-sufficiency.
insights.locator: Myco hopes to successfully appeal the Patreon decision

insights.claim: The stated market gap is translation, not information: published LSD synthesis schematics from Albert Hofmann and Sasha Shulgin already exist but read as hieroglyphics to non-chemists, so video demonstration is the actual unlock.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: The same logic applies broadly — dangerous knowledge becomes accessible not when it is published but when it is demonstrated in accessible media formats.
insights.quote: Sure, a chemist can go get a synthesis schematic and synthesize LSD, but for the average Joe it would look like hieroglyphics
insights.locator: In mid-2023 he started drawing up plans

insights.claim: Supporters frame the project as building crowdsourced, decentralized access models for controlled substances, with a generation of cultivators having learned mushroom growing from these videos — an install base that persists after any single channel is removed.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Knowledge diffusion is irreversible once the cohort is trained; removing the source does not remove the capability from the market.
insights.quote: At the heart of what he is doing is creating crowdsourced, decentralized access models for these substances.
insights.locator: His Robin Hood ethos has seen him pick up supporters

insights.claim: The creator's originating grievance was gatekeeping cliquishness on drug forums like Shroomery, Mycotopia and Nexus, which a Shroomery moderator concedes exists and can shut down people with new ideas.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Hostile incumbent communities generate their own disruptors; forum gatekeeping created the mass-market educator that displaced them.
insights.quote: They treated new cultivators and chemists like shit

insights.claim: The flagship LSD video shows a greenish-blue liquid but conducts no on-camera test to confirm the substance's identity, despite being marketed as '100 percent pure LSD' — the central claim is unverified within the artifact itself.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Unverified DIY synthesis instructions carry direct user-harm liability, which is precisely the exposure platforms are moving to eliminate.
insights.quote: the video shows his chemist collaborator holding out a lab flask of a greenish-blue liquid, but no test of the substance is conducted on camera to confirm its identity

insights.claim: Psychedelic chemistry expert Hamilton Morris publicly stated with absolute certainty that the product is not 100 percent pure LSD, flagging the unprecedented green-blue color as immediately suspicious.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Expert rebuttal within the same subculture is the only functioning quality control here — there is no institutional verification layer.
insights.quote: The fact it has this green-blue color is something that I have never heard of. Right off the bat that is a bit suspicious.
insights.locator: But some are calling bullshit on Myco’s methods

insights.claim: Open-sourcing drug production draws threats from incumbent producers, with a June 2024 text warning that releasing the LSD video could hurt a lot of people's business and create problems nobody wants.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Disintermediating an illicit supply chain carries violent enforcement risk that legal disruptors never face — a distinct cost of operating in gray markets.
insights.quote: Tell Willy putting out a video like that can hurt a lot of people's business and that can make problems nobody wants
insights.locator: Myco's commitment to democratizing making drugs

insights.claim: The creator's operational security is now physical as well as digital — permanent face mask in all photos and videos, withheld surname, and carrying a gun everywhere in Puerto Rico.
insights.speaker: Mattha Busby
insights.so_what: Pseudonymous operation is the load-bearing structure of this business; identity exposure, not policy enforcement, is the existential risk.
insights.quote: I carry a gun everywhere I go.
insights.locator: Myco is increasingly security-conscious as a result
